Empirical Research Plan: “Does Acquirer Size Causally Depress Announcement-Date Returns in U.S. M&A, 1980-2001?”

-----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Design: Cross-sectional matching / weighting estimator combined with saturated regression adjustment (a “doubly-robust” inverse-probability-weighted regression).  
Rationale:  

• We need the causal effect of being a “large” versus “small” acquirer on the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) earned at the takeover announcement.  
• Size is not randomly assigned.  However, we observe rich pre-deal firm and deal covariates that capture the main economic forces simultaneously correlated with both size and announcement returns (valuation, leverage, liquidity, payment method, deal type, etc.).  
• Under the Conditional Independence Assumption (CIA) – i.e., after conditioning on those observables and on time- and industry-fixed effects – the remaining variation in size is as-good-as random.  
• Using a doubly-robust estimator (propensity-score overlap weighting OR inverse-probability weighting plus regression) gives consistent ATT/ATE if either (i) the propensity-score model OR (ii) the outcome equation is correctly specified.  It also handles different support between large and small acquirers better than simple matching.  
• Event-study CARs are already purged of normal return co-movements, so they serve as quasi-experimental “shocks” that occur over a three-day window, alleviating reverse timing issues.  

Secondary designs (robustness):  
a) Within-firm fixed-effects regression among firms that make ≥2 acquisitions and cross size quintiles over time – exploits intra-firm variation and controls for time-invariant unobservables (managerial talent, governance).  
b) Continuous-treatment dose-response (generalized propensity score) on log(Assets) to ensure results are not driven by arbitrary quintile cut-points.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable:  LARGE_i,t  = 1 if the acquirer’s total assets (Compustat, FYE-1) place it in the top two size quintiles of all NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ firms in that calendar year; 0 otherwise.

Control group:  SMALL_i,t  = bottom three size quintiles.

Unit of observation: individual acquisition i announced on day τ by acquirer k in calendar year t.

Timing: Size (and all covariates) measured as of the most recent fiscal year-end preceding the announcement; thus covariates are predetermined relative to the CAR window (-1 to +1).

-----------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-----------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Conditional Independence (Unconfoundedness)  
CAR_i  ⟂  LARGE_i  |  X_i, Year_t FE, 2-digit SIC FE  
Plausibility: We observe essentially the full set of firm- and deal-level determinants documented in the mergers literature (payment method, relative size, target form, Q, leverage, cash).  Remaining unobservables (manager overconfidence, board quality) are less obviously correlated with assets once we absorb firm FE in the within-firm version.

A2. Common Support / Overlap  
0 < P(LARGE=1|X) < 1.  The size distributions of firms doing deals overlap on many covariates; diagnostics (love plots) can check this.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption (SUTVA)  
The CAR of one acquirer is not affected by whether another firm is large. Reasonable given short, firm-specific event windows.

A4. No Anticipation / Clean Event Window  
The market does not systematically learn about the deal before day ‑1 for large or small firms differentially.  Using a (-5,+5) window as robustness cushions minor information leaks.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigation
-----------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Unobserved Managerial Hubris/Governance correlated with Size.  
Mitigation:  
• Include governance proxies when available (insider ownership, board independence).  
• Firm fixed-effects estimator for repeat acquirers to remove time-invariant managerial style.

T2. Differences in Deal Type / Industry Merger Waves.  
Mitigation:  
• Explicitly control for payment, target status, relative size, and 2-digit SIC × year FE.  
• Re-weight large and small samples so covariate distributions match (overlap weighting).

T3. Heteroskedasticity and Mechanical Scaling (CAR × size).  
Mitigation:  
• Report both percentage CARs and dollar gains (CAR × market cap).  
• Cluster standard errors at the acquirer level (and two-way with calendar year in robustness).

-----------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-----------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---------------- 0. Packages ----------------
library(data.table)      # fast data wrangling
library(dplyr)
library(MatchIt)         # matching / propensity scores
library(sandwich)        # robust vcov
library(lmtest)          # coeftest
library(ipw)             # inverse-prob weighting
library(fixest)          # fast high-dim FE regressions
# install.packages("WeightIt")  # for overlap weights

# ---------------- 1. Load Data ----------------
car   <- fread("car_event_window.csv")        # CAR_i: [-1,+1]
comp  <- fread("compustat_vars.csv")          # size, Q, leverage...
sdc   <- fread("sdc_deals.csv")               # deal attributes

# Merge
dat <- sdc %>% 
  left_join(comp, by = c("gvkey","fyear")) %>%
  left_join(car,  by = c("permno","ann_date")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(CAR))                         # keep deals with CAR

# ---------------- 2. Treatment Construction ---
# Compute size quintiles by calendar year
dat <- dat %>% group_by(year) %>% 
  mutate(size_rank = ntile(total_assets, 5),
         LARGE = as.integer(size_rank >= 4)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Controls
dat <- dat %>% mutate(
  log_assets = log(total_assets),
  rel_size   = deal_value / mkt_cap_pre,
  cash_dummy = (payment_method == "Cash"),
  stock_dummy= (payment_method == "Stock"),
  targ_public= (target_status == "Public"),
  industry   = substr(sic,1,2)
)

# ---------------- 3. Propensity-Score Overlap Weighting ------------
library(WeightIt)
w <- weightit(LARGE ~ log_assets + TobinsQ + leverage + cash_flow +
                rel_size + cash_dummy + stock_dummy + targ_public +
                factor(year) + factor(industry),
              data = dat, method = "overlap")

dat$w_overlap <- w$weights

# ---------------- 4. Doubly-Robust Outcome Regression --------------
dr_mod <- lm(CAR ~ LARGE + log_assets + TobinsQ + leverage + cash_flow +
                   rel_size + cash_dummy + stock_dummy + targ_public +
                   factor(year) + factor(industry),
             data = dat, weights = w_overlap)

coeftest(dr_mod, vcov = vcovHC(dr_mod, type = "HC2"))["LARGE",]

# ---------------- 5. Within-Firm FE Robustness ---------------------
multi <- dat %>% group_by(permno) %>% filter(n() >= 2)
fe_mod <- feols(CAR ~ LARGE + rel_size + cash_dummy + stock_dummy +
                       targ_public + TobinsQ + leverage |
                       permno + year + industry,
                data = multi, cluster = "permno")
summary(fe_mod)

# ---------------- 6. Balance Check ----------------
library(cobalt)
love.plot(w, binary = "std")   # standardized mean diffs

# ---------------- 7. Output Dollar Gains ----------------
dat <- dat %>% mutate(dollar_gain = CAR * mkt_cap_pre)
lm_dollar <- lm(dollar_gain ~ LARGE + controls..., data=dat)
```

-----------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Theory and prior descriptive evidence suggest β_LARGE < 0.  
Magnitude: Small acquirers post ≈ +1.0 % CAR (-1,+1), large acquirers ≈ 0 % or slightly negative.  I therefore expect an ATT of roughly –1 to –1.5 percentage points, economically meaningful relative to an unconditional mean near zero.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = satisfied, 0 = weak)
a) Rich covariate set for CIA ................. 0.8  
b) Common support diagnostics ................. 1.0  
c) Correct functional form in either PS or Y .. 0.8  
d) No violation of SUTVA / interference ....... 1.0  
e) Proper inference (cluster, FE, HC) ......... 1.0  

Total (out of 5) = 4.6 → strong but still relies on CIA; within-firm FE helps.
